previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and anxiety was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and one episode of coffee ground emesis. She was initially managed in the ICU with IV access via femoral line due to difficulty with peripheral access. A CT scan showed esophageal wall thickening and pneumobilia, but no acute abdominal process. An upper endoscopy revealed no active bleeding, with erosions at the gastroesophageal junction attributed to retching. The coffee ground emesis was determined to be from a small Mallory-Weiss tear. Her insulin regimen was adjusted during fasting, with Lantus held initially and later resumed at her home dose of 20 units. Electrolyte imbalances, including hypokalemia and hypophosphatemia, were corrected. Anxiety-related tachycardia improved with reassurance and transfer to the medicine floor. She tolerated oral intake, was weaned off IV support, and discharged home on her baseline medications with follow-up plans for glucose and electrolyte monitoring.

TECHNIQUE:  Single frontal radiograph of the chest.

now reaches the low SVC.  The lungs remain clear.  No pneumothorax or

surface contours are normal, though the extreme right lateral surface is
partially excluded from the field of view.

microbiology.comments: Feces negative for C. difficile toxin A & B by EIA.            (Reference Range-Negative).

NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.
